full_judgment:
Md. Rezaul Hasan J : This Rule under section 561 A of the Code of Criminal Procedure (the Code), at the instance of the accused petitioner, has been issued calling upon the opposite party to show cause as to why the proceeding of the Special Case No.18 of 2007, corresponding to ACC GR No. 25 of 2007 arising out of Motijheel Police Station Case No. 140 (3) 2007 dated 29-3-2007 under section 409/109 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, should not be quashed and/or such other or further order or orders passed as to this Court may seem fit and proper. 

 2. Prosecution case is that one Mr. Saiful Alam, Assistant Director of the Anti-Corruption Commission (the ACC) has lodged an FIR, registered as Motijheel Police Station Case No. 140 dated 29-3-2007 with Motijheel Police Station against-12 accused persons alleging, amongst other that upon the approval of the then Minister of the Ministry of Housing and Works, the said Ministry,vide a Memo No. শা-১০/১এম-২/২০০০(খন্ড-১)৫৬ dated 27-1-2004 directed Rajdhani Unnayan Kotripokkha (RAJUK) to sell out 13 (thirteen) abandoned houses after evaluating the market price; that thereafter, the Ministry of Housing and Works vide Memo No. শা-১০/১এম-২/২০০(অংশ-৩)১৪৮ further directed to take steps to sell out other 16(sixteen) abandoned houses; that RAJUK at the direction of the Ministry of Housing and Works .constituted a Price Evaluation Committee and a Tender Committee for sale; that the said Price Evaluation Committee submitted its evaluated price, which RAJUK had sent to the Ministry of Housing and Works for approval; that the then Minister of the Ministry of Housing and Works, i.e. accused No. 1 approved the evaluated price even though the price so evaluated was not proper; that the Ministry of Housing and Works vide Memo No. শা-১০/১এম-২/২০০০(অংশ-৩)৪৩৯ dated 21- 10-2004 approved 17 (seventeen) abandoned houses for sale at the evaluated price recommended by the said Price Evaluation Committee and one house at the tender price to the highest bidder and directed RAJUK for floating fresh notice for tender in respect of the rest of the houses; that the accused No.1 allegedly having approved the price fixed by the Price Evaluation Committee for sale of the said 18 abandoned houses has caused loss to the Government and thus committed an offence under section 5(2) of the said Act of 1947, sections 409/109 of the Penal Code read with section 15 of the said Ordinance (in fact there is no such section 15 and 15 (Ka) of the Emergency Powers Ordinance, 2007. From this FIR has arisen ACC GR Case No. 25 of 2007. 

 3. The accused petitioner was not named is the FIR and no case has been stated against him in the FIR. 

 4. That a Deputy Director of the ACC, took up investigation and having found a primafacie case he has submitted Charge sheet No. 535/Cha dated 20-9-2007, under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code, 1861 and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947 read with Rule 15 of the Emergency powers Rule, 2007, against 13 (thirteen) persons. This time impleading the petitioner as the accused No. 13 with the allegation committing offence under section 109 of the Penal Code, i.e. for abetment. 

 5. That, thereafter the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge vide Order No.6 dated 24-10- 2007 directed to register 14 (fourteen) different cases in respect of the said charge sheets, numbered respectively as Metro Special Case Nos. 116 (ক)/ 2007, 116(খ)/2007, 116(গ)/2007, 116(ঘ)/2007. 116 (ঙ)/2007, 116(চ)/2007, 116(ছ)/2007, 116(জ)/ 2007. 116(ঝ)/2007, 116(হ)/2007, 116(ট)/2007, 116 (ঠ)/2007, 116(ড)/2007 and 116(ঢ)/2007. 

 6. That, the Court of Metropolitan Senior Special Judge, in the said Metro Special Case No. 116(ঝ)/2007, vide order dated 25-10-2007 took cognizance of the offence against the petitioner and others, under sections 409/109 of the Penal Code and section 5(2) of the Prevention of Corruption Act, 1947. He has transferred the said Metropolitan Special Case No. 116(ঝ)/2007 to the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka for trial, wherein it has been renumbered as Special Case No. 18 of 2007. 

 7. Thereafter the said Court vide order dated 17-2-2008 framed charge against, amongst others, the petitioner in the said case. Charges were framed against the petitioner under section 409 of Penal Code read with section 109 of Penal Code. . 

 9. Mr. Yousuf Hossain Humayun, learned Senior Advocate with Mr. Ahsanul Karim, with Mr. Khairul Alam Chowdhury, with Mr. Aminul Haque, and Mr. Tanvir Hossain Khan, learned advocates appearing for the accused petitioner, having placed the petition before us fi led under section 561 A of the Code along with the annexures submits (1) that the petitioner was not named is the FIR as because he has not committed any offence (2) that, the allegations made in 'the charge sheet against this petitioner, if considered in its entirety and accepted to be true, the same does not disclose any offence under section 409/109 of the Penal Code;(3) that, neither any case of entrustment nor any case of abetment has been stated in the charge sheet against this petitioner; (4) that, the buyer of the property in question was Accom-Engineering Ltd., not this petitioner; (5) that the sale of shares of the said company upon revaluation is permissible under the law as well as the same has not been treated as an offence under any of the law of the land and (6) that, in two other similar cases being Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26562 of 2009 and 26563 of 2009 respectively, arose out of the similar transaction, the proceedings have been quashed by the High Court Division. Thus, the learned lawyer maintains that the case stated against the petitioner is wholly misconceived, does not disclose any offence, oppressive and vexations, hence liable to be quashed. 

 10. The learned Advocate Mr. Khurshid Alam Khan, appearing on behalf of the Opposite Party No.2 i.e. Anti-Corruption Commission (ACC) with leave of the Court, mainly submits that the charge sheet clearly discloses offence against the petitioner under section 409/109 of the Penal Code. He next submits that the accused petitioner has been charge sheeted by the ACC and the case is virtually a bundle of facts which are to be proved before the trial Court by adducing evidence. Accordingly, the learned advocate for the ACC submits that the interference under 561 A of the Code is not called for at this stage, hence he prayed for discharging the Rule. 

 12. The FIR case has been recorded herein before. 

 16. Thereafter, as recorded in the charge sheet, বাড়ীটি একম ইঞ্জিনিয়ারিং এন্ড কোম্পানী লিঃ এর নামে ১৬-১০-২০০৬ ইং তারিখে লিজ দলিল সম্পন্ন হয়, যার নম্বর-৯৬০৪। Admittedly, the company of the petitioner having acquired ownership (as lessee) in respect of the demised property, the question of entrustment of the said property in favour of the lessee company or the petitioner is simply absurd, misconceived and baseless. 

 17. As to the question of earning profit of Tk. 316.54 lac in 10 days by transferring 100% shares in the lessee company, it is to be noted that as defined in section 2, sub section (7) of the Sale of goods Act. 1930 share comes with the definition of 'goods' and is a transferable the asset. There is no law that prohibits transfer of shares by the holder of shares. except under section 27A of the Bank Companies Act, 1991, which requires that the shares of a director of a debtor company cannot be transferred without obtaining prior permission of the lender bank. There is no such case before us. On the other hand. section 38 of the Companies Act. 1994. permits transfer of shares by the share-holders of a company, following the procedure laid dawn in that section. Only obligation, consequent upon transfer of shares, is to notify the Registrar of the Joint Stock Companies and Firms, by submitting Form-XII and schedule-X, if any change does occur in the Board of Directors or in the share-holding position of the company. Similarly. Companies Act perm its re-valuation of shares, upon acquisition or diminution :' loss of assets by the company. On the same principle, company can allot further shares at par. below per or above par/at premium. The only question that may arise following transfer of shares is the question of capital gain or loss, as to be treated under the provisions of the Income Tax Ordinance, 1984. ACC has no authority nor any scope to raise question such transaction. 

 21. The ACC, in this process, even could have implicated the subsequent buyer of the shares as abettor, which they did not for the obvious reason that the act of transfer of shares or of any other property acquired by valuable and lawful consideration does not, in any way, constitutes any offence in the eye of law. So, both transferor and the transferee of the demised property or of the shares should be kept out of this case as was done in lodging FIR. Besides, the mere act of buying any property at a lower price or selling at a higher price is no offence, unless the very transaction itself is banned by any law. 

 22. We have had the benefit to consult the judgment and order dated 15-10-2010 passed in the Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26562 of 2009 and also Criminal Miscellaneous Case No. 26563 of 2009 in which Special Case No. 24 of 2007 and 25 of 2007 have been quashed. Those tow proceedings were also initiated by the ACC out of similar transaction. We do not find any reason to depart from the views expressed in those two Miscellaneous Cases. 

 In the result, the Rule is made absolute and the impugned proceeding of the Special Case No.18 of 2007 corresponding to ACC GR No. 25 of 2007 arising out of Motijheel Police Station Case No. 140(3) 2007 dated 29-3-2007 under section 409/109 of the Penal Code, now pending in the Court of Special Judge, Court No.3, Dhaka, is hereby quashed, so far it relates to the petitioner is concerned.
